title: Linkability of student submission data

title: Direct identifiability of student
description: Student ID is explicitly transmitted in the submission flow, making the student directly identifiable from this data flow alone.

title: Unauthorized disclosure during transmission
description: Assignment work file, student ID, course information, and submission timestamp could be intercepted if the connection between student and web app is not properly secured (e.g., missing HTTPS/TLS encryption).

title: Data aggregation across submissions
description: Multiple assignment submissions from the same student across different courses and time periods can be aggregated to reveal patterns about academic performance, workload, study habits, and potential vulnerabilities.
assumptions: System retains historical submission data that can be combined

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of what data is collected during submission, how long it is retained, who has access to it, or how it may be used beyond grading purposes.

title: Potential non-compliance with educational privacy regulations

description: The flow includes requesting role and student ID, creating evidence that could prevent students from denying their involvement in submission requests. This non-repudiation capability may be a privacy threat if students cannot control or deny attribution of their actions.
